⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Please stop using the microwave immediately and do not reset the fuse box again; repeated tripping indicates a serious fault that could cause fire or electric shock. The fact that it trips the whole kitchen circuit when you press start suggests an internal short circuit, most likely in the magnetron (the part that generates heat) or the high-voltage capacitor. It is also possible there is a fault with the door interlock switches causing a live-to-earth leak. Because this involves mains electricity and high-voltage components inside the casing, you must not open it yourself. To help narrow down if it's purely an overload issue versus a hard short: is the microwave plugged into its own dedicated socket, or is it sharing that plug with other appliances like a kettle? Regardless of the answer, please arrange for a qualified appliance engineer to inspect it before using it again.
